subject: chemistry
title: Reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium — AQA GCSE Chemistry (8462) specification, section 4.6.2.
meta_desc: GCSE Chemistry (AQA) practice covering Reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium, specification section 4.6.2.
final_note: You worked through Reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium — 25 specification statements.

concepts.def: A reaction in which the products of the reaction can react to produce the original reactants. Once some product has formed it is able to change back into the starting substances, so the change is not a one-way dead end.

The double arrow used to represent a reversible reaction, written A + B ⇌ C + D. It shows that the change can run in the forward direction and in the reverse direction; it does not say how much of each substance is present.
The specification's example of a reversible reaction: ammonium chloride ⇌ ammonia + hydrogen chloride. Heating the white solid gives the two gases, and cooling the gases forms the white solid again.

Blue hydrated copper(II) sulfate loses water on heating to give white anhydrous copper(II) sulfate, taking energy in. Adding water to the white solid gives the blue solid again and releases the same amount of energy.
Apparatus which prevents the escape of reactants and products, so that everything made by the forward reaction stays in the mixture and is available for the reverse reaction.

The state reached in a closed system when the forward and reverse reactions occur at exactly the same rate. Both reactions are still happening, so the amounts of the substances stay constant rather than becoming equal.

A description of the relative amounts of reactants and products present at equilibrium. Moving towards the products is called shifting to the right; moving towards the reactants is shifting to the left.

The idea that if a system is at equilibrium and a change is made to any of the conditions, the system responds to counteract the change. It is used to predict the effect of changes on systems at equilibrium.
The system shifts in the direction that opposes what was done to it, reducing the effect of the change without cancelling it completely, so the new equilibrium is different from the original one.

If the concentration of a reactant is increased, more products are formed until equilibrium is reached again; if the concentration of a product is decreased, more reactants react until equilibrium is reached again.

Raising the temperature increases the relative amount of products for an endothermic reaction and decreases it for an exothermic reaction. Lowering the temperature has the opposite effect in each case.

For gaseous reactions, an increase in pressure shifts the equilibrium position towards the side with the smaller number of molecules, and a decrease in pressure shifts it towards the side with the larger number.

concepts.term: Counting molecules from the symbol equation
concepts.def: The numbers of gas molecules on each side of an equilibrium are read from the balancing numbers in the symbol equation, so 2SO2 + O2 ⇌ 2SO3 has three molecules on the left and two on the right.

mcqs.q: Which statement describes what makes a reaction a reversible reaction?
options: The products of the reaction can react to produce the original reactants
The reaction goes fully forwards and then it goes fully backwards
The reaction finishes with equal amounts of reactants and products
The reaction can be made faster or slower by a change of conditions
mcqs.explain: This is the definition given in the specification: in some chemical reactions the products can react to produce the original reactants.

mcqs.q: A reversible reaction is represented as A + B ⇌ C + D. What does the ⇌ symbol tell you?
options: That the mixture holds equal amounts of A, B, C and D throughout it
That the reaction can go in the forward and the reverse direction
That the mixture has already reached equilibrium at every moment
That the forward reaction is faster than the reverse reaction
mcqs.explain: The double arrow is the way the specification represents a reversible reaction: A and B can form C and D, and C and D can form A and B.

mcqs.q: A sample of blue hydrated copper(II) sulfate is heated and turns white. What must be done to turn it blue again?
options: Nothing will work, as the direction is fixed once heating has started
Heat the white solid much more strongly for a longer period of time
Add water to the white solid, changing the conditions back again
Grind the white solid to a powder to raise its surface area
mcqs.explain: The direction of reversible reactions can be changed by changing the conditions; adding water reverses the change that heating produced.

mcqs.q: Ammonium chloride ⇌ ammonia + hydrogen chloride is given as an example of a reversible reaction. White ammonium chloride is heated in a tube and the two gases form. Which statement about this example is correct?
options: The ammonium chloride has been destroyed for good
Half of the solid always stays behind unchanged
The two gases must react first, before the solid heats
Cooling the gases re-forms ammonium chloride
mcqs.explain: The products react to produce the original reactant, which is what makes this the specification's example of a reversible reaction.

mcqs.q: The forward reaction of a reversible reaction is exothermic. What can be said about the reverse reaction?
options: It is exothermic as well and transfers the same amount of energy back
It is endothermic and transfers the same amount of energy as the forward one
It is endothermic but it transfers less energy than the forward one
It is endothermic and the energy transferred depends on the rate
mcqs.explain: If a reversible reaction is exothermic in one direction it is endothermic in the opposite direction, and the same amount of energy is transferred.

mcqs.q: Heating blue hydrated copper(II) sulfate to form white anhydrous copper(II) sulfate and water takes in 45 kJ of energy. Water is then added to the white solid. What happens to the energy?
options: Less than 45 kJ is given out, because some energy is lost as heat
45 kJ is taken in, because this change also needs energy
45 kJ is given out, as the same amount of energy is transferred
Most of the 45 kJ is given out, but some is always lost
mcqs.explain: The reverse reaction is exothermic and, as the specification states, the same amount of energy is transferred in each case.

mcqs.q: A reversible reaction takes place in a sealed flask. When is the mixture at equilibrium?
options: When both the forward and the reverse reactions have completely stopped
When the amounts of all the reactants and of all the products are the same
When all of the reactants have been converted into the products
When the forward and reverse reactions occur at exactly the same rate
mcqs.explain: This is the specification's definition of equilibrium in apparatus which prevents the escape of reactants and products.

mcqs.q: Why must a reversible reaction be carried out in apparatus that prevents reactants and products escaping if equilibrium is to be reached?
options: Escaped products cannot take part in reverse reactions
The reverse reaction happens anyway, whatever escapes
Equilibrium means nothing at all is allowed to move about
The reactants and products must be present in equal amounts
mcqs.explain: The reverse rate can only rise to match the forward rate if the products stay in the mixture, so escape prevents equilibrium.

mcqs.q: The same reversible reaction is allowed to reach equilibrium at two different temperatures. What can be said about the amounts of the substances present?
options: The amounts must be equal at equilibrium whatever conditions are used
The amounts depend only on how quickly equilibrium was reached
The relative amounts of the reactants and products depend on the conditions
The amounts are fixed by the masses that were mixed at the start
mcqs.explain: The specification states that the relative amounts of all the reactants and products at equilibrium depend on the conditions of the reaction.

mcqs.q: A system at equilibrium has one of its conditions changed. According to the specification, how does the system respond?
options: It responds until the change made to it has been cancelled out completely
It stays exactly as it was, because it is already at equilibrium
It stops reacting until the original conditions are restored
It responds in the direction that counteracts the change that was made
mcqs.explain: If a system at equilibrium has a condition changed, the system responds to counteract the change.

mcqs.q: What can Le Chatelier's Principle be used for?
options: Predicting the effect of changing conditions on a system at equilibrium
Calculating the exact amount of each product present at the new equilibrium
Predicting how long a given mixture will take to reach equilibrium again
Showing that heating a reaction always increases its yield
mcqs.explain: The effects of changing conditions on a system at equilibrium can be predicted using Le Chatelier's Principle.

mcqs.q: In a sealed flask N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g). The forward reaction is exothermic. More nitrogen is pumped into the flask at constant temperature. What is the qualitative prediction?
options: Less ammonia is present at the new equilibrium
More ammonia forms at the new equilibrium
The amount of ammonia present cannot change
Ammonia forms faster but its amount is fixed
mcqs.explain: Increasing the concentration of a reactant means more products are formed until equilibrium is reached again.

mcqs.q: The concentration of one substance in a mixture at equilibrium is changed. What happens to the concentrations of the other substances?
options: Only the substance whose concentration was altered is different
They stay the same, as the system is always at equilibrium
They change only when the temperature is altered as well
They all change until equilibrium is reached again in the mixture
mcqs.explain: The system is no longer at equilibrium, and the concentrations of all the substances change until equilibrium is reached again.

mcqs.q: For the equilibrium CH3COOH + C2H5OH ⇌ CH3COOC2H5 + H2O, more ethanol (C2H5OH) is added. What happens?
options: More products form until equilibrium is reached again in the flask
More reactants form, because ethanol was added to the reactant side
Nothing changes at all, since the total mass has not altered
The reaction speeds up but no extra ester is being formed
mcqs.explain: If the concentration of a reactant is increased, more products will be formed until equilibrium is reached again.

mcqs.q: In the equilibrium 2SO2 + O2 ⇌ 2SO3, sulfur trioxide (SO3) is continuously removed from the mixture. What happens?
options: More reactants form, because there is now less product present
More reactants react until equilibrium is reached again
Nothing happens, because the system stays at equilibrium
The mixture ends up holding equal amounts of each one
mcqs.explain: If the concentration of a product is decreased, more reactants will react until equilibrium is reached again.

mcqs.q: A sealed flask holds an equilibrium mixture of hydrogen, iodine and hydrogen iodide: H2 + I2 ⇌ 2HI. Extra hydrogen is injected and the flask is left until equilibrium is reached again. What is found?
options: Less HI, and more iodine than there was before
The same HI and the same iodine as before
More HI, and less iodine than there was
Only the hydrogen is now at a higher level than before
mcqs.explain: Increasing a reactant concentration forms more product, and forming more HI uses up some of the iodine.

mcqs.q: The forward reaction of a reversible reaction is endothermic. The temperature of the system at equilibrium is increased. What happens to the relative amount of products?
options: It increases, because the reaction is endothermic in the forward direction
It decreases, because raising the temperature will release more energy
It decreases, because the reactants are used up much more quickly
It stays the same, because heating changes only the reaction rates
mcqs.explain: The relative amount of products at equilibrium increases for an endothermic reaction when the temperature is increased.

mcqs.q: The forward reaction of a reversible reaction is exothermic. The temperature of the system at equilibrium is increased. What happens to the relative amount of products?
options: It increases, because the forward reaction is the exothermic one
It decreases, because the forward reaction gives out energy
It increases, since heating always improves any yield
It stays the same, since heating changes only the rates
mcqs.explain: The relative amount of products at equilibrium decreases for an exothermic reaction when the temperature is increased.

mcqs.q: The forward reaction of a reversible reaction is endothermic. The temperature of the system at equilibrium is decreased. What happens to the relative amount of products?
options: It increases, as cooling a mixture always drives the reaction onwards
It increases, as the system must give out energy when it cools down
It decreases, as the endothermic direction is no longer favoured
It stays the same, as cooling only slows both reactions down
mcqs.explain: The relative amount of products at equilibrium decreases for an endothermic reaction when the temperature is decreased.

mcqs.q: The forward reaction of a reversible reaction is exothermic. The temperature of the system at equilibrium is decreased. What happens to the relative amount of products?
options: It decreases, as a cooler mixture must form less product
It decreases, as the endothermic direction is favoured
It stays the same, as cooling alters only the two rates
It increases, as the forward reaction is exothermic
mcqs.explain: The relative amount of products at equilibrium increases for an exothermic reaction when the temperature is decreased.

mcqs.q: For 2NO2 ⇌ N2O4 the forward reaction is exothermic. A sealed tube of the mixture is placed in iced water and the brown colour of NO2 fades. What does this show?
options: Cooling has stopped both of the reactions in the sealed tube
Cooling has increased the relative amount of the product N2O4
Cooling has moved the equilibrium towards the reactant NO2
Cooling has slowed the forward reaction down only
mcqs.explain: Lowering the temperature increases the relative amount of products for an exothermic reaction, so the brown NO2 is used up.

mcqs.q: For the gaseous equilibrium N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g), the pressure is increased. Which way does the equilibrium position shift?
options: Towards nitrogen and hydrogen, the side with more molecules
Neither way, as pressure cannot alter this mixture
Towards the ammonia, the side with the fewer molecules
Towards the nitrogen, which has heavier molecules
mcqs.explain: An increase in pressure shifts the position towards the side with the smaller number of molecules: four on the left, two on the right.

mcqs.q: For the gaseous equilibrium 2SO3(g) ⇌ 2SO2(g) + O2(g), the pressure is decreased. Which way does the equilibrium position shift?
options: To the left, towards the side with just two gas molecules
Neither way, since the numbers of atoms are equal here
Neither way, as pressure changes only alter rates
To the right, the side with three molecules of gas
mcqs.explain: A decrease in pressure shifts the position towards the side with the larger number of molecules: two on the left, three on the right.

mcqs.q: A student is given the equilibrium H2(g) + I2(g) ⇌ 2HI(g), all gases, and increases the pressure on the sealed vessel. What should the student predict?
options: No shift, as each side has two molecules
A shift to the right, towards the hydrogen iodide
A shift to the left, towards hydrogen and iodine
A shift to the side with the heavier molecules
mcqs.explain: The sides have equal numbers of gas molecules, so neither side is favoured by a change in pressure.
